turns.text: ok be honest can u quiz me on heart chambers and blood flow. i have my index cards out the color ones banded by body system. house finally quiet after the picnic at delgado park with andre aaliyah and deshawn but i gotta wrap up before the kids need dinner

Happy to. Let's go from your cards. Start here: trace one drop of blood, starting when it comes back from the body into the heart. Name each chamber, valve and vessel in order. Take your time, then type it out and I'll mark it.
ok so vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary artery, lungs. then pulmonary vein, left atrium, bicuspid?, left ventricle, aorta

Nearly perfect. Fixes:

- Bicuspid is also called the mitral valve. You had it right.
- You skipped the aortic valve between the left ventricle and the aorta.

Full loop: vena cava → right atrium → tricuspid → right ventricle → pulmonary valve → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium → mitral → left ventricle → aortic valve → aorta → body.

Quick one: which side has the thicker wall, and why?

left bc it pushes to the whole body. lol i got that one off the card. i was supposed to do these in lot c last week but the van was making me late so i just did them in the car and half of it didnt stick

Correct on the left side. It pumps against much higher pressure, so it needs more muscle.

Since the car session didn't stick, a trick: the right side only goes to the lungs, the left side goes everywhere else. Next one: which vessels carry oxygen-rich blood to the heart, and which carry oxygen-poor blood away from it?
pulmonary veins bring the oxygen rich in. pulmonary artery takes poor out. weird that its backwards from normal
Exactly right. Arteries go away from the heart, veins go toward it, whatever the oxygen level. That's the rule to put on the card.
